title: Catch a faulty calculator
brief: The calculator may use V instead of V², omit the one-half factor, or accept negative speed. Specify tests that distinguish these errors.
supplied: Does the drag implementation obey its declared contract?

rho = 1.2 kg/m³
V = 20 m/s
S = 10 m²
Cd = 0.04 dimensionless
Test outcomes and which fault each case catches.
Quasi-steady supplied coefficients. Change only the declared independent quantity; other inputs remain fixed.
This is a bounded teaching calculation. It does not establish aircraft safety, successful takeoff, or behavior outside the specified condition.
A single check at zero speed cannot distinguish all faulty implementations.
At V=20 drag=96 N; doubling speed gives ratio=4.
Show controls with units, supplied and student results separately, a result trace, and a clear limitation.

Supplied executable experiment recipe:
For each V in [0, 10, 20, 30, 40]:
  configured output = 0.5*rho*V*S*Cd
  comparison = 0.5*rho*V^2*S*Cd
Return the paired values with the declared units.

The app uses the arithmetic evaluator in src/core/onboarding/expression.js. It supports +, -, *, /, ^ and parentheses; it never evaluates an equation as JavaScript.
Accept only implementations passing all three checks.

checks.message: This case catches a missing one-half factor.
This test distinguishes quadratic from linear speed scaling.
The contract requires rejection of negative speed.

hints: One baseline case cannot distinguish every faulty implementation.
A doubled-speed case detects a missing square; negative speed probes rejection.
The baseline is 96 N, doubling speed gives a factor of four, and negative speed must be rejected.
